pairs.long: Everyone at school starts wearing the same sneakers and slang, so Ben changes his own style to match the group.

pairs.label: Deindividuation
pairs.short: Lost in a roaring crowd, Ty yells things he'd never say alone.
pairs.long: Anonymous in a roaring stadium crowd, Ty loses self-awareness and yells things he would never say when he is alone.

pairs.label: Door-in-the-Face Technique
pairs.short: Ava asks for a $500 jacket, then happily accepts $20.
pairs.long: Ava first asks her parents for a $500 jacket, and after they say no, she asks for just $20 instead.

pairs.label: Foot-in-the-Door Technique
pairs.short: Cal asks for help with one math problem, then the whole packet.
pairs.long: Cal asks a friend to help with one math problem, and once she agrees, he asks her to do the whole packet.

pairs.label: Groupthink
pairs.short: Desire for harmony makes group members suppress dissent and decide badly.
pairs.long: A phenomenon in which the desire for group harmony leads members to suppress dissenting opinions and make flawed decisions.

pairs.label: Halo Effect
pairs.short: One positive impression of a person makes you assume other good traits.
pairs.long: A bias in which one positive impression of someone shapes judgments of their other traits, like assuming attractive people are kind.

pairs.label: Social Loafing
pairs.short: In a group project, Max puts in less effort than usual.
pairs.long: In a group project where individual contributions aren't tracked, Max puts in much less effort than he would alone.

pairs.label: Superordinate Goals
pairs.short: Objectives rival groups can only reach by cooperating, which reduces conflict.
pairs.long: Shared objectives that require different or rival groups to work together to achieve them, often reducing conflict between those groups.

pairs.label: Displacement
pairs.short: Scolded by his boss, Ken snaps at his little sister.
pairs.long: After being scolded by his boss, Ken holds in his anger and then snaps at his innocent little sister at home.

pairs.label: Id
pairs.short: Primitive, unconscious part of personality that demands immediate gratification of urges.
pairs.long: The primitive, unconscious part of personality that operates on the pleasure principle, seeking immediate gratification of basic drives and desires.

pairs.label: Projection
pairs.short: Mara dislikes her coworker but insists the coworker dislikes her.
pairs.long: Mara secretly dislikes her coworker, but she insists that her coworker is the one who dislikes her.

pairs.label: Rationalization
pairs.short: After cheating, Joe explains that everyone does it so it's fine.
pairs.long: After cheating on a quiz, Joe builds a reasonable-sounding explanation that everyone does it, so it isn't really wrong.

pairs.label: Reaction Formation
pairs.short: Nora secretly likes Jake but acts cold and mean toward him.
pairs.long: Nora has a secret crush on Jake, so she hides her true feelings by acting cold and mean toward him.

pairs.label: Sublimation
pairs.short: Redirecting unacceptable impulses into socially acceptable, productive activities.
pairs.long: A defense mechanism in which unacceptable impulses are channeled into socially acceptable or productive activities, like turning aggression into athletics.

pairs.label: Superego
pairs.short: Lena feels guilty after keeping extra change, hearing an inner voice.
pairs.long: Lena feels guilty after keeping extra change from a cashier, as her internalized sense of right and wrong objects.

pairs.label: Unconditional Positive Regard
pairs.short: A therapist accepts and values her client without judgment, whatever he does.
pairs.long: According to Rogers, a therapist accepts and values her client without judgment or conditions, regardless of his behavior or feelings.

pairs.label: Conscientiousness
pairs.short: Ivy makes a color-coded schedule and meets every deadline early.
pairs.long: Ivy creates a color-coded schedule for her group project, sets deadlines, and reliably finishes everything before they arrive.

pairs.label: Neuroticism
pairs.short: Wes overthinks every text and always expects the worst outcome.
pairs.long: Wes overthinks every casual text for hours, feels anxious and moody, and always expects the worst-case scenario.

pairs.label: Reciprocal Determinism
pairs.short: Thoughts, behavior, and environment all continuously influence one another.
pairs.long: Bandura's idea that a person's thoughts, behavior, and environment constantly interact, and each of these factors also shapes the others.

pairs.label: Self-Efficacy
pairs.short: Ria is confident she can ace her upcoming driver's test.
pairs.long: Ria believes strongly in her own ability to succeed at this specific task, so she is confident she'll ace her driver's test.

pairs.label: Approach-Avoidance
pairs.short: Kai wants to attend the party but dreads seeing his ex.
pairs.long: Kai really wants to attend the weekend party but dreads that his ex will be there, leaving him with mixed feelings.

pairs.label: Boredom Susceptibility
pairs.short: Intolerance for repetitive, monotonous experiences and a craving for novelty.
pairs.long: A component of sensation seeking marked by an intolerance for repetitive or monotonous experiences and a strong desire for novelty and change.

pairs.label: Homeostasis
pairs.short: The body's tendency to maintain a stable internal environment, such as temperature.
pairs.long: The body's tendency to maintain a stable internal environment by regulating conditions such as temperature, hunger, and hydration.

pairs.label: Incentive Theory
pairs.short: Mark studies extra hours because his parents promised him the car.
pairs.long: Mark puts in extra hours of studying because his parents promised him the car if he earns an A.

pairs.label: Intrinsic Motivation
pairs.short: Lila paints for hours purely because she enjoys it.
pairs.long: Lila paints for hours with no prize or grade involved, simply because the activity itself is personally rewarding and enjoyable.

pairs.label: Yerkes-Dodson Law
pairs.short: Moderate nerves sharpen Jo's test performance, but panic makes her freeze.
pairs.long: Moderate pre-test nerves sharpen Jo's focus and performance, but intense panic overwhelms her and makes her perform worse.

pairs.label: Display Rules
pairs.short: Rae smiles and thanks her aunt for an ugly sweater.
pairs.long: Rae forces a big smile and thanks her aunt for an ugly sweater, because her culture expects polite emotions.

pairs.label: Facial-Feedback Hypothesis
pairs.short: Forcing a smile during a bad mood actually lifts Tom's mood.
pairs.long: Tom is in a bad mood, but forcing himself to smile makes him feel a little happier because expressions influence emotions.

sets.label: Unit 4: Social Psychology and Personality (Set 2)
sets.title: Unit 4 Quilt: Social Psychology and Personality (Set 2)

pairs.label: Actor-Observer Bias
pairs.short: Ben blames traffic for his own lateness but calls others careless.
pairs.long: When Ben is late, he blames traffic, but when his teammates are late, he decides they are careless and unreliable.

pairs.label: Dispositional Attributions
pairs.short: Kai explains a classmate's rudeness by saying, 'He's just a mean person.'
pairs.long: Kai explains a classmate's rude comment by pointing to internal characteristics, like his personality or attitude, rather than the situation.

pairs.label: Downward Social Comparison
pairs.short: After a bad quiz, Ana feels better remembering others scored even lower.
pairs.long: After a bad quiz, Ana boosts her self-esteem by thinking about classmates who did even worse than she did.

pairs.label: External Locus of Control
pairs.short: Jay thinks his grades depend on luck and the teacher's mood.
pairs.long: Jay believes his grades are determined by outside forces such as luck, fate, and other people rather than his own actions.

pairs.label: Optimistic Explanatory Style
pairs.short: After failing a quiz, Ria thinks, 'That's temporary and just this test.'
pairs.long: After failing a quiz, Ria sees the setback as temporary, limited to this test, and caused by outside factors.

pairs.label: Pessimistic Explanatory Style
pairs.short: After failing a quiz, Sam thinks, 'I'm hopeless at everything, forever.'
pairs.long: After failing a quiz, Sam sees the setback as permanent, widespread, and caused by his own flaws.

pairs.label: Situational Attributions
pairs.short: Lia blames her friend's low grade on the noisy testing room.
pairs.long: Lia explains her friend's low grade by pointing to outside circumstances, like a noisy testing room, rather than his ability.

pairs.label: Upward Social Comparison
pairs.short: Watching a star athlete, Lou feels motivated to train harder.
pairs.long: Lou measures himself against a more successful athlete, which motivates him to improve but may also lower his self-esteem.

pairs.label: Belief Perseverance
pairs.short: Clinging to a conclusion even after its supporting evidence has been disproved.
pairs.long: The tendency to hold onto a conclusion even after the evidence that supported it has been discredited or contradicted.

pairs.label: Discrimination
pairs.short: A landlord refuses to rent to a family because of their religion.
pairs.long: A landlord refuses to rent an apartment to a qualified family solely because of their religion, an example of unjustified unequal treatment.

pairs.label: Implicit Attitudes
pairs.short: Despite saying she's unbiased, Ana subtly avoids sitting near certain classmates.
pairs.long: Ana sincerely says she holds no biases, yet hidden feelings toward certain classmates quietly influence her behavior without her awareness.

pairs.label: In-Group Bias
pairs.short: Coach Lee always picks players from his own old school.
pairs.long: Coach Lee gives playing time and favorable treatment to players from his own alma mater over equally talented players from other schools.

pairs.label: Prejudice
pairs.short: Before meeting any new neighbors, Dee assumes they will be unfriendly.
pairs.long: Dee holds a negative preconceived attitude toward a whole category of people, with no personal experience or sufficient evidence.

pairs.label: Central Route to Persuasion
pairs.short: Lena carefully weighs a sunscreen ad's research evidence before deciding.
pairs.long: Before buying, Lena carefully analyzes the quality of the arguments and evidence in a sunscreen ad and then forms her attitude.

pairs.label: Collectivism
pairs.short: Cultural emphasis on community and family needs over self-interest.
pairs.long: A cultural orientation that emphasizes cooperation and the needs of the community or family over self-interest.

pairs.label: False Consensus Effect
pairs.short: Dan assumes everyone shares his taste in music and politics.
pairs.long: Dan overestimates how many people share his tastes, opinions, and values, assuming almost everyone agrees with him.

pairs.label: Group Polarization
pairs.short: After talking together, a debate team's views become far more extreme.
pairs.long: After discussing an issue, teammates who already leaned one way end up holding much more extreme views than they would alone.

pairs.label: Individualism
pairs.short: Cultural emphasis on personal independence, goals, and self-reliance.
pairs.long: A cultural orientation that emphasizes personal independence, individual goals, and self-reliance over obligations to others.

pairs.label: Informational Social Influence
pairs.short: Unsure which fork to use, Ava copies diners who clearly know.
pairs.long: In an unfamiliar, ambiguous situation, Ava follows what others do because she assumes they know the right thing to do.

pairs.label: Normative Social Influence
pairs.short: Though he privately disagrees, Ben claps along to fit in.
pairs.long: Although he privately disagrees with the crowd, Ben goes along with it in order to be liked and accepted.

pairs.label: Obedience
pairs.short: Following direct commands or orders from an authority figure.
pairs.long: A form of compliance in which people follow direct commands or orders from an authority figure, even against their own judgment.

pairs.label: Peripheral Route to Persuasion
pairs.short: Tom buys sunscreen because a famous, attractive actor smiles in the ad.
pairs.long: Tom buys a sunscreen because a famous, attractive actor endorses it, swayed by superficial cues rather than the quality of the arguments.

pairs.label: Social Facilitation
pairs.short: Performing simple, well-practiced tasks better, and hard tasks worse, around others.
pairs.long: The tendency to perform better on simple or well-practiced tasks, but worse on difficult or unfamiliar tasks, when others are present.

pairs.label: Denial
pairs.short: Despite clear test results, Jo insists she is perfectly healthy.
pairs.long: Despite a doctor's clear diagnosis, Jo refuses to acknowledge or accept the painful reality and insists nothing is wrong.

pairs.label: Ego
pairs.short: The rational part of personality operating on the reality principle.
pairs.long: The rational part of personality that follows the reality principle, balancing inner urges and moral demands with what is realistic.

pairs.label: Projective Tests
pairs.short: A psychologist shows ambiguous inkblots and asks what Rae sees.
pairs.long: A psychologist presents ambiguous inkblots and asks Rae to interpret them, hoping to reveal her hidden thoughts and feelings.

pairs.label: Regression
pairs.short: Stressed by exams, seventeen-year-old Mo starts sucking his thumb again.
pairs.long: Under intense stress, seventeen-year-old Mo reverts to earlier, more childlike behaviors, like sucking his thumb or throwing tantrums.

pairs.label: Repression
pairs.short: Lena automatically pushes a painful childhood memory out of her awareness.
pairs.long: A defense mechanism in which Lena automatically pushes distressing thoughts and memories out of her conscious awareness without realizing it.

pairs.label: Self-Actualizing Tendency
pairs.short: Eli feels an inner drive to grow into his full potential.
pairs.long: According to humanistic psychology, Eli has an innate drive to grow, develop, and reach his full potential.

pairs.label: Unconscious
pairs.short: The part of the mind holding thoughts and desires outside awareness.
pairs.long: In Freud's theory, the part of the mind containing thoughts, memories, desires, and conflicts outside awareness that still influence behavior.

pairs.label: Agreeableness
pairs.short: Nora is warm, trusting, and always willing to cooperate with others.
pairs.long: Nora is compassionate, trusting, and friendly, and she cooperates easily, scoring high on this Big Five trait.

pairs.label: Extraversion
pairs.short: Cam is talkative, assertive, and gains energy from parties and crowds.
pairs.long: Cam loves being around people, speaks up confidently, and gains energy from social interaction, scoring high on this Big Five trait.

pairs.label: Openness to Experience
pairs.short: Zia is curious, imaginative, and eager to try unfamiliar ideas and activities.
pairs.long: Zia is curious and creative, loves imagining new possibilities, and is willing to try unfamiliar ideas, foods, and activities.

pairs.label: Approach-Approach
pairs.short: Choosing between two great scholarships, Kim loves both offers equally.
pairs.long: Kim must choose between two equally appealing scholarship offers, a motivational conflict between two desirable options.

pairs.label: Arousal Theory
pairs.short: Bored on a quiet Sunday, Roy seeks a thrilling roller coaster.
pairs.long: Roy is understimulated, so he seeks a thrilling activity to raise his alertness to his optimal level, while stressed people seek calm.

pairs.label: Extrinsic Motivation
pairs.short: Kira reads only because her parents pay her five dollars per book.
pairs.long: Kira reads books only to earn the money her parents pay her, doing it for an outside reward rather than for enjoyment.

pairs.label: Self-Determination Theory
pairs.short: Ms. Cruz boosts autonomy, competence, and connection so students want to learn.
pairs.long: Ms. Cruz gives students choices, builds their skills, and fosters connection, meeting needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness that nurture inner drive.

pairs.label: Cannon-Bard Theory
pairs.short: Seeing a bear, Ana's racing heart and fear occur simultaneously.
pairs.long: Seeing a bear, Ana's racing heart and her conscious feeling of fear occur at the same time, independently of each other.

pairs.label: James-Lange Theory
pairs.short: Leo notices his heart racing first, then concludes he must be afraid.
pairs.long: Leo first notices his heart pounding and his hands trembling, and only then interprets that bodily reaction as fear.

pairs.label: Two-Factor Theory
pairs.short: Jax's racing heart feels like love because he is on a date.
pairs.long: Jax feels a racing heart after a roller coaster, but because his date is beside him, he labels the feeling as attraction.

sets.label: Unit 5: Mental and Physical Health (Set 1)
sets.title: Unit 5 Quilt: Mental and Physical Health (Set 1)

pairs.label: Eustress
pairs.short: Positive stress that boosts motivation, performance, or well-being.
pairs.long: A positive form of stress that enhances motivation, performance, or well-being, like the excited energy before a big game.

pairs.label: Exhaustion Stage
pairs.short: After months of relentless pressure, Maya's depleted body gets sick.
pairs.long: After months of relentless pressure, Maya's resources run out, leaving her depleted, unable to cope, and often sick.

pairs.label: Fight-Flight-Freeze Response
pairs.short: Spotting a bear, Cole's heart pounds as his body prepares to react.
pairs.long: Spotting a bear, Cole's heart pounds as his body automatically readies him to confront the danger, escape, or stay still.

pairs.label: Problem-Focused Coping
pairs.short: Overwhelmed by homework, Ari makes a schedule to tackle the actual workload.
pairs.long: Overwhelmed by homework, Ari attacks the source of her stress by making a schedule and breaking assignments into steps.

pairs.label: Tend and Befriend Theory
pairs.short: Under stress, Gwen seeks her peers' support and comforts her cousin.
pairs.long: Under stress, Gwen copes by seeking support from her peers and protecting and nurturing her little cousin.

pairs.label: Gratitude
pairs.short: Positive emotion from recognizing and appreciating kindness or support received from others.
pairs.long: A positive emotional response that comes from recognizing and appreciating the benefits, kindness, or support you have received from others.

pairs.label: Posttraumatic Growth
pairs.short: After surviving a serious illness, Dee feels stronger and values life more.
pairs.long: After struggling through a life-threatening illness, Dee reports newfound inner strength and a deeper appreciation for life.

pairs.label: Resilience
pairs.short: After losing her job, Rosa adapts quickly and keeps functioning.
pairs.long: After losing her job, Rosa adapts to the setback, recovers quickly, and keeps functioning well despite the stress.

pairs.label: Subjective Well-Being
pairs.short: A person's self-reported evaluation of their own happiness and life satisfaction.
pairs.long: A person's self-reported evaluation of their happiness and life satisfaction, including the balance of positive and negative emotions.

pairs.label: Diathesis-Stress Model
pairs.short: An inherited vulnerability only becomes a disorder after overwhelming life pressures.
pairs.long: Mental disorders result when a biological or psychological predisposition is triggered by overwhelming life pressures.

pairs.label: Dysfunction
pairs.short: Thoughts, emotions, or behaviors that interfere with daily functioning.
pairs.long: A criterion for psychological disorders: thoughts, emotions, or behaviors that interfere with a person's ability to handle daily life effectively.

pairs.label: Eclectic Approach
pairs.short: Treatment that combines techniques from multiple therapies based on the individual's needs.
pairs.long: A flexible style of treatment that combines techniques and principles from multiple perspectives or therapies, depending on each person's needs.

pairs.label: Stigma
pairs.short: Employers avoid hiring Cam after learning he was treated for depression.
pairs.long: After learning Cam was treated for depression, employers avoid hiring him because of a negative label attached to mental disorders.

pairs.label: Agoraphobia
pairs.short: Fear of being trapped keeps Ida from leaving home for crowded places.
pairs.long: Ida fears situations where escape might be difficult, so she avoids crowded and open places and rarely leaves home.

pairs.label: Ataque de Nervios
pairs.short: Culture-bound syndrome in Latin American cultures: shouting, trembling after family crisis.
pairs.long: A culture-bound syndrome common in Latin American cultures, with episodes of shouting, crying, and trembling after a stressful family event.

pairs.label: Catatonic Stupor
pairs.short: Hal sits motionless and unresponsive, though his eyes are open.
pairs.long: Hal sits completely motionless and unresponsive, appearing awake with his eyes open, but does not react to anything around him.

pairs.label: Compulsions
pairs.short: Uma feels driven to wash her hands exactly twenty times.
pairs.long: Uma feels driven to wash her hands exactly twenty times, a ritual that briefly eases the anxiety from her obsessive thoughts.

pairs.label: Delusions
pairs.short: Strongly held false beliefs that persist despite clear evidence to the contrary.
pairs.long: Strongly held false beliefs that persist despite clear evidence otherwise, commonly associated with psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia.

pairs.label: Dissociative Amnesia
pairs.short: After a traumatic event, Cora cannot recall important personal information.
pairs.long: After a traumatic event, Cora cannot recall key personal information, a memory loss inconsistent with ordinary forgetting or injury.

pairs.label: Flashbacks
pairs.short: A veteran suddenly feels as though he is reliving combat.
pairs.long: Triggered by a loud noise, a veteran has a vivid, intrusive experience of reliving a traumatic combat event.

pairs.label: Flat Affect
pairs.short: Ned shows almost no emotion in his face, voice, or gestures.
pairs.long: Ned shows little or no outward emotion through his facial expressions, tone of voice, or gestures, a negative symptom.

pairs.label: Generalized Anxiety Disorder
pairs.short: Fay feels continually tense and worried about everything for months.
pairs.long: Fay is continually tense and apprehensive, worrying about grades, health, and the future for months with no specific trigger.

pairs.label: Hallucinations
pairs.short: False sensory experiences, like hearing voices that aren't actually there.
pairs.long: A positive symptom of schizophrenia involving false sensory experiences, such as hearing voices or seeing things that are not actually present.

pairs.label: Hypervigilance
pairs.short: Since the accident, Gus constantly scans every room for danger.
pairs.long: Since his accident, Gus sits facing the door and constantly scans every room for threats, always on high alert.

pairs.label: Mania
pairs.short: Abnormally elevated mood and energy, with impulsivity and little need for sleep.
pairs.long: A state of abnormally elevated mood, energy, and activity that can include impulsivity, decreased need for sleep, and impaired judgment.

pairs.label: Panic Attack
pairs.short: With no danger present, Jax's heart pounds and he can't breathe.
pairs.long: With nothing dangerous happening, Jax is overwhelmed by sudden intense fear, a pounding heart, and shortness of breath that peak within minutes.

pairs.label: Taijin Kyofusho
pairs.short: A man in Japan fears his body odor will offend others.
pairs.long: A man in Japan is intensely afraid his appearance or body odor will offend or embarrass the people around him.

pairs.label: Word Salad
pairs.short: Lee's speech is a jumble of terms that make no sense together.
pairs.long: Lee's speech is strung together incoherently, such as 'purple elephant tree yesterday pizza,' making communication unintelligible.

pairs.label: Active Listening
pairs.short: A therapist carefully reflects and clarifies a client's feelings to show empathy.
pairs.long: A humanistic therapist carefully reflects and clarifies the client's thoughts and feelings so the client feels understood and accepted.

pairs.label: Biofeedback
pairs.short: Using electronic monitoring to gain voluntary control over processes like heart rate.
pairs.long: A technique that uses electronic monitoring to help people gain voluntary control over processes such as heart rate or muscle tension.

pairs.label: Cognitive Restructuring
pairs.short: A therapist helps Ian replace 'I always fail' with realistic thoughts.
pairs.long: A therapist helps Ian identify and challenge his negative thought 'I always fail,' and replace it with more realistic, adaptive thoughts.

pairs.label: Dream Interpretation
pairs.short: A therapist analyzes symbols in Eve's sleeping visions to uncover unconscious conflicts.
pairs.long: A psychodynamic therapist analyzes the content and symbols of Eve's visions while she sleeps to uncover her unconscious thoughts and conflicts.

pairs.label: Electroconvulsive Therapy
pairs.short: Brief electrical currents trigger a seizure to relieve severe depression.
pairs.long: Under anesthesia, a patient with severe depression receives electrical currents to the brain that trigger a brief seizure.

pairs.label: Free Association
pairs.short: Sol says whatever thoughts and memories come to mind without censoring himself.
pairs.long: In therapy, Sol openly says whatever thoughts, feelings, and memories come to mind without censoring them, letting unconscious conflicts surface.

pairs.label: Lithium
pairs.short: A mood stabilizer that reduces manic episodes in bipolar disorder.
pairs.long: A mood-stabilizing medication, a naturally occurring mineral, commonly used to reduce the severity of manic episodes and help prevent mood swings.

pairs.label: Lobotomy
pairs.short: A historic surgery cut nerves linking the frontal lobes to emotional centers.
pairs.long: Once used to calm violent or uncontrollably emotional patients, this surgery cut nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the brain's emotional centers.

pairs.label: Systematic Desensitization
pairs.short: Ben pairs relaxation with gradual exposure to spiders, starting with photos.
pairs.long: To overcome his spider phobia, Ben pairs relaxation with gradual exposure, from photos up to a real spider.

pairs.label: Tardive Dyskinesia
pairs.short: After years on antipsychotic medication, Pat develops involuntary, repetitive facial movements.
pairs.long: After years of taking antipsychotic medication, Pat develops involuntary, repetitive movements of the face and tongue as a side effect.

pairs.label: Token Economies
pairs.short: Students earn points for good behavior and trade them for privileges.
pairs.long: In a classroom program, students earn a point for each desired behavior and later exchange the points for privileges or treats.

pairs.label: Therapeutic Alliance
pairs.short: The collaborative, trusting relationship between therapist and client that supports treatment.
pairs.long: The collaborative, trusting bond between therapist and client that supports effective treatment and positive outcomes.

sets.label: Unit 5: Mental and Physical Health (Set 2)
sets.title: Unit 5 Quilt: Mental and Physical Health (Set 2)

pairs.label: Alarm Stage
pairs.short: Moments after learning of a layoff, Jun's heart races and hormones surge.
pairs.long: The moment Jun learns of a layoff, his body recognizes the stressor and surges, the first phase of the adaptation sequence.

pairs.label: Emotion-Focused Coping
pairs.short: Facing a layoff, Mia calls a friend to vent and calm down.
pairs.long: Mia can't change her layoff, so she manages her feelings by venting to a friend, meditating, and calming down.

pairs.label: Health Psychology
pairs.short: A specialist helps patients quit smoking, exercise, and cope with chronic illness.
pairs.long: This branch studies and promotes behaviors like exercising, quitting smoking, and coping that influence who stays well or becomes ill.

pairs.label: Hypertension
pairs.short: Chronically elevated blood pressure that raises cardiovascular risk.
pairs.long: A condition of chronically elevated blood pressure that increases the risk of cardiovascular disease and other health problems.

pairs.label: Immune Suppression
pairs.short: Reduced activity of the body's defenses, making infection more likely.
pairs.long: A reduction in the activity or effectiveness of the body's defenses against infection, leaving it more vulnerable to illness.

pairs.label: Resistance Stage
pairs.short: Weeks into a stressful project, Raj manages well but stays tense.
pairs.long: Weeks into a demanding project, Raj has adapted and keeps functioning, but his body remains physiologically activated and on alert.

pairs.label: Courage
pairs.short: Despite her fear, Dani speaks up against the bully.
pairs.long: Despite being terrified, Dani persists and stands up to a bully, showing bravery and willingness to act despite fear.

pairs.label: Positive Psychology
pairs.short: Study of strengths, good feelings, and what helps people flourish.
pairs.long: The branch of the field that studies human strengths, good feelings, and the factors that contribute to happiness and flourishing.

pairs.label: Transcendence
pairs.short: Standing under the stars, Omar feels connected to something far larger.
pairs.long: Standing under a starry sky, Omar appreciates beauty, finds deep meaning, and feels connected to something larger than himself.

pairs.label: Wisdom
pairs.short: Mr. Park uses experience and knowledge to give sound advice in conflicts.
pairs.long: Mr. Park thinks critically, draws on knowledge and life experience, and makes sound judgments when students bring him difficult conflicts.

pairs.label: Ageism
pairs.short: A manager rejects a talented applicant solely for being sixty-two.
pairs.long: A manager refuses to hire a highly qualified applicant solely because she is sixty-two, showing prejudice based on age.

pairs.label: Biopsychosocial Model
pairs.short: A doctor treats Sam's back pain by addressing body, mood, and relationships.
pairs.long: A doctor explains Sam's back pain as the result of interacting biological, psychological, and social factors, so treatment targets all three.

pairs.label: Deviation from Social Norms
pairs.short: A man's behavior is so unusual for his culture that neighbors worry.
pairs.long: One criterion for identifying a psychological problem is when thoughts or behaviors are far outside what a culture accepts and expects.

pairs.term: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM)
pairs.label: DSM
pairs.short: The standard handbook clinicians use to classify and diagnose conditions by criteria.
pairs.long: The primary handbook that psychologists and psychiatrists in the United States use to classify and diagnose psychological conditions using standardized criteria.

pairs.label: Acrophobia
pairs.short: Climbing a ladder, Tess freezes in intense, irrational terror of heights.
pairs.long: Tess experiences intense, irrational fear whenever she is high off the ground, such as on a ladder or a balcony.

pairs.label: Anorexia Nervosa
pairs.short: Severe food restriction, intense fear of weight gain, and distorted body image.
pairs.long: An eating condition marked by severe restriction of food intake, an intense fear of gaining weight, and a distorted body image.

pairs.label: Antisocial Personality Disorder
pairs.short: Rex repeatedly lies, breaks the law, and shows no remorse for victims.
pairs.long: Rex shows a persistent pattern of deceit, impulsivity, and violating others' rights, with no remorse for the people he hurts.

pairs.label: ADHD
pairs.short: Despite trying hard, Kyle cannot sit still, loses focus, and acts impulsively.
pairs.long: Kyle shows a persistent pattern of trouble staying focused, constant fidgeting, and impulsive actions that interferes with school and daily life.

pairs.label: Autism Spectrum Disorder
pairs.short: Leo struggles with back-and-forth conversation and strongly prefers repetitive routines.
pairs.long: Leo has persistent difficulty with social communication and interaction, along with restricted interests and repetitive patterns of behavior.

pairs.label: Bipolar I Disorder
pairs.short: Tori has had a full manic episode, sometimes followed by deep lows.
pairs.long: Tori has had at least one full manic episode of extreme energy, which may be followed by episodes of deep lows.

pairs.label: Borderline Personality Disorder
pairs.short: Cleo's mood, self-image, and relationships swing wildly, with intense fear of abandonment.
pairs.long: Cleo shows instability in mood, self-image, and relationships, along with impulsive behavior and an intense fear of being abandoned.

pairs.label: Bulimia Nervosa
pairs.short: Recurrent binge eating followed by attempts to compensate and prevent weight gain.
pairs.long: An eating condition marked by recurrent episodes of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors intended to prevent weight gain.

pairs.label: Dissociative Identity Disorder
pairs.short: Sasha shifts between two distinct selves, with memory gaps between them.
pairs.long: Sasha has two or more distinct selves that take turns controlling her behavior, along with gaps in memory between them.

pairs.label: Dopamine Hypothesis
pairs.short: Theory: schizophrenia symptoms are tied to excess activity of one neurotransmitter.
pairs.long: A theory linking schizophrenia's psychotic symptoms to excessive activity of one particular neurotransmitter in certain brain pathways.

pairs.label: Hoarding Disorder
pairs.short: Walt cannot discard old items, and clutter has filled every room.
pairs.long: Walt has persistent difficulty throwing away possessions, regardless of their value, and the resulting clutter interferes with daily living.

pairs.label: Major Depressive Disorder
pairs.short: For two weeks, Gia has felt hopeless and lost interest in everything.
pairs.long: For at least two weeks, Gia has had a persistently low mood and lost pleasure in activities, significantly impairing her daily functioning.

pairs.label: Narcissistic Personality Disorder
pairs.short: Vic constantly demands admiration, exaggerates his importance, and ignores others' feelings.
pairs.long: Vic has an inflated sense of self-importance, a constant need for admiration, and little empathy for the people around him.

pairs.label: Obsessions
pairs.short: Kat can't stop picturing intrusive, unwanted images of her house burning.
pairs.long: Kat is plagued by persistent, intrusive, unwanted thoughts and images, such as her house burning down, that cause intense anxiety.

pairs.label: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
pairs.short: Months after a car crash, Joel relives it and avoids driving.
pairs.long: After surviving a car crash, Joel has intrusive memories of it, avoids driving, and feels constantly on guard.

pairs.label: Social Anxiety Disorder
pairs.short: Priya dreads speaking in class, fearing classmates will judge and embarrass her.
pairs.long: Priya feels intense fear in situations where others might judge, embarrass, or scrutinize her, so she avoids speaking up in class.

pairs.label: Antianxiety Drugs
pairs.short: Prescribed for constant tension, these medicines calm Rosa's central nervous system.
pairs.long: Rosa's doctor prescribes medicines that reduce her symptoms of constant tension and worry by calming the central nervous system.

pairs.label: Antidepressants
pairs.short: Ben's medicine alters mood-related neurotransmitter activity to lift his symptoms.
pairs.long: A doctor prescribes Ben a medicine that eases his persistently low mood, and sometimes anxiety, by altering mood-related neurotransmitter activity.

pairs.label: Antipsychotic Medications
pairs.short: Medicine that reduces seeing and believing things that aren't real.
pairs.long: Gil takes a medicine that eases symptoms like seeing things that aren't there and false beliefs by changing a key neurotransmitter.

pairs.label: Applied Behavior Analysis
pairs.short: A therapist rewards a child each time he makes eye contact.
pairs.long: A therapist uses reinforcement and other learning-based techniques to build a child's helpful skills, like eye contact, and reduce disruptive actions.

pairs.label: Aversion Therapies
pairs.short: To curb smoking, a clinic pairs cigarettes with an unpleasant nausea-inducing taste.
pairs.long: To reduce his smoking, a clinic repeatedly pairs cigarettes with an unpleasant stimulus, creating a negative association with the habit.

pairs.label: Cognitive Triad
pairs.short: Sol thinks he's worthless, the world is hostile, and the future bleak.
pairs.long: In Beck's approach, Sol's negative thoughts about himself, the world, and the future form a pattern that feeds his low mood.

pairs.label: Cognitive-Behavioral Therapies
pairs.short: A therapist helps Mia change distorted thoughts and the habits sustaining them.
pairs.long: To treat Mia's panic, a therapist works on changing her maladaptive thought patterns and the habits that keep the problem going.

pairs.label: Deinstitutionalization
pairs.short: Replacing long-term psychiatric hospital stays with community-based treatment.
pairs.long: The movement to replace long-term psychiatric hospital stays with community-based care let many people receive treatment outside large facilities.

pairs.label: Hypnosis
pairs.short: Under a therapist's guidance, Lia enters a focused, highly suggestible state.
pairs.long: A therapist guides Lia into a state of focused attention and increased suggestibility to help her manage symptoms or explore thoughts.

pairs.label: Person Centered Therapy
pairs.short: A therapist offers empathy, genuineness, and acceptance, trusting Jo to grow.
pairs.long: Following Carl Rogers, a therapist offers Jo empathy, genuineness, and total acceptance so she can reach her full potential.
